before.existing_compacted_memory: Alice settled Node 20 (B6, S8, W11) and roaded toward Node 10. Goals: Secure Node 21 or 33/34 to obtain Wheat/Ore, balancing the current Wood/Brick/Sheep heavy start. Bob (Nodes 12, 43) has high-yield O/W/S and is competing for Node 11/21; expect early Dev Cards/Cities from him. Charlie (Nodes 41, 14) has balanced resources and is targeting coastal ports (Node 7/15/42). Alice is last to place second settlement.

existing_relationship_updates.note: Alice holds a grudge against Bob for a 'stunt' in a previous game and distrusts his 'neighborly' claims.
Alice holds a grudge/warning against Charlie from a previous game trade.
Charlie is acting cautiously to avoid conflict between Alice and Bob.
Bob targeted Alice with the robber on Hex 4 and stole from her, intensifying the existing grudge.

old_notes_to_compact.note: Bob has heavy Wheat production now (Node 43: Wh9, Wh6). He's likely aiming for a City or Dev card strategy early. I must secure Node 33 or 34 to compete on Ore/Wheat.
Bob has a strong O/W/S setup (Nodes 12 and 43). He will likely dominate Dev Cards. I must prioritize my second settlement at a high-yield Ore/Wheat spot like 21 or 33 to stay competitive.
Settled node 25 for O/W/S balance. Bob is heavy on wheat. I should watch for his early development card plays.
Road placed toward node 26 to secure the Ore port. This will be essential for trading my high Ore yield from node 25.
Settled Node 20 and 25. Strong balance of resources. Robber is on the Desert (10).
Bought a dev card. Node 9 is open and provides a 3:1 port, which is a good target for the road extending from node 20. Bob is still the primary threat with his wheat production.
Used Road Building to reach node 9 (3:1 port) and node 21. Priority is to settle node 9 once I have the resources. Node 11 is blocked by Bob's settlement at 12.

Nodes 9 (3:1 port) and 32 (Wheat) are my next expansion targets. I need Wood, Brick, and Wheat to settle node 9. Node 21 is blocked by my own settlement at 20, so I must go to 32 if I expand that way.

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: Bob rolled a 7. He has 3 wheat and might be looking to build or buy a dev card after the rob. My node 20 (Sheep 8, Brick 6) is a high-value target.
Bob moved the robber to Hex 4 (Sheep 8) and stole from me. He currently has 4 wheat and whatever he stole from me. My priority is clearing Hex 4 to restore my sheep income.

relevant_chat.message: Smart move, Charlie. Probably wise to stay out of the splash zone while Bob tries to convince me he's being neighborly.
I think I'll take this spot by the mountains. I'm going to need a bit more than just wood and brick if I'm going to keep up with Bob's 'scenic' wheat empire.
A little port access should help balance things out later. It's good to have options when the dice don't go your way.
A 'wheat empire' has a nice ring to it, Alice! But with all that ore you're gathering, I think I'm the one who should be worried about keeping up.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say. Good luck, everyone—though maybe a little less for you, Bob.
Ouch, Alice! I thought we left the past in the past. But hey, if the dice are listening to you, I might be in for a long afternoon.
A little investment in the future shouldn't hurt. Let's see if the deck is feeling generous today.
Just putting down some infrastructure. Having a few more paths open never hurt, and that coastal view at 9 looks much better than being stuck in the middle of Bob's wheat fields.

Well, the roads are down, but I'm still a bit short on the supplies to actually get those outposts running. Charlie, you seem to have a surplus of wood over there—if you're looking for some wool to keep warm on that coast, let me know. Bob, I'm watching those wheat fields of yours.
Watching them? Alice, I'd say they're more like community gardens. Plenty of room for everyone... eventually!
I might be able to spare some timber for the right price, Alice. Let's see how the next roll treats us.
Sorry, Alice. You've been watching my wheat so closely, I figured I'd give you something else to keep an eye on. Those sheep were looking a bit too comfortable anyway.
Can't blame you, Charlie. It's much more peaceful down there!
Gotta make sure I have a clear path to expand. That 42 direction looks like it'll open up some good options later on.
I'll take the 8-3-4 up here. I definitely need some wood if I'm going to keep up with you two, and it keeps me from getting totally boxed in down south.
Heading toward the coast. A little sea breeze and some port access should keep things interesting.
I'll take the scenic route down by the fields at 43. All that wheat should keep me busy while you two keep an eye on each other.
Just going to tuck this road in toward the coast. A little fresh air and a view of the sea never hurt anyone, right?
Hey, I can't blame you for wanting a sea view! It's much quieter out there than in the hustle and bustle of the wheat fields anyway.
Community gardens, exactly! I'm just here to make sure nobody goes hungry. Let's see if the land is ready to provide.
